parsed.summary: Lean asserts two existence claims. First, some smooth, divergence-free, rapidly decaying u₀ on ℝ³ has no global, jointly smooth, finite-energy unforced Euler solution. Second, some nonzero, compactly supported such u₀ has a solution v in an all-order L²-Sobolev class on [0,T*), with 0<T*<1, uniformly bounded energy, and closed-interval solutions existing exactly for T<T*; v has locally bounded C¹ norm and locally finite ∫‖curl v‖_∞, while limsup_{t↑T*}(‖v‖_∞+‖∇v‖_∞)=∞ and ∫_0^{T*}‖curl v‖_∞ dt=∞. This also yields the global nonexistence. The main caveat is that the blow-up quantity is the full C¹ norm rather than ‖∇u‖_∞ alone; given the asserted energy bound, a Gagliardo–Nirenberg interpolation makes the two equivalent, so this is a literal but not substantive gap.

glossary.note: Applied only to smooth fields, so the fderiv junk value never arises.

glossary.plain: Additionally, for all m and K: |D^m u₀(x)| ≤ C(1+|x|)^{-K}
(v,p) jointly C^∞ on ℝ³×[0,∞); ∂_t v + (v·∇)v = −∇p and ∇·v = 0 for t ≥ 0; v(·,0) = u₀
Additionally, v(t) ∈ L² for each t and sup_t ‖v(t)‖₂² < ∞
L² class of f, or 0 if f ∉ L²
glossary.note: The fallback is never used, because MemLp is required wherever toL2 appears.

glossary.plain: For t ∈ I: v(t) is C^∞ and all D^m v(t) ∈ L²; t ↦ D^m v(t) is continuous into L² on I
Solution on I in that class: ∇·v = 0; v(0) = u₀; p(t) differentiable for interior t; the strong L² time derivative w is in the same class; w + (v·∇)v = −∇p at interior times
glossary.note: This is an H^∞ class rather than classical C^∞ in (t,x). The paper's 'smooth solution' class is not specified in the excerpt.

glossary.plain: curl v, with components ω_i = ∂_{i+1}v_{i+2} − ∂_{i+2}v_{i+1} (indices cyclic in Fin 3)

glossary.note: The paper's blow-up quantity is ‖∇u‖_∞ alone.

lean_claims.plain: There is a smooth, divergence-free u₀ with all derivatives rapidly decaying such that no pair (v,p) is a jointly smooth global solution of unforced Euler on ℝ³×[0,∞) with v(t) ∈ L² and uniformly bounded energy.

There exist u₀, T*, v, p with the following properties. (1) u₀ is smooth, divergence-free, rapidly decaying, compactly supported and nonzero. (2) 0 < T* < 1. (3) (v,p) solves Euler in the H^∞ class on [0,T*), with sup_t ‖v(t)‖₂² < ∞. (4) For every T > 0, an H^∞-class solution with datum u₀ exists on [0,T] iff T < T*. (5) For each T < T*, sup_{[0,T]}(‖v‖_∞+‖∇v‖_∞) < ∞ and ∫_0^T ‖curl v‖_∞ < ∞. (6) limsup_{t↑T*}(‖v(t)‖_∞+‖∇v(t)‖_∞) = ∞. (7) ∫_0^{T*} ‖curl v‖_∞ dt = ∞. (8) u₀ admits no global smooth finite-energy solution.

paper_claims.plain: There exists u₀ ∈ C_c^∞ with ∇·u₀ = 0 and 0 < T*(u₀) < ∞ whose smooth solution satisfies limsup_{t↑T*} ‖∇u(t)‖_∞ = ∞ and ∫_0^{T*} ‖curl u‖_∞ dt = ∞.

coverage.why: Matches up to two points: C¹-norm blow-up instead of ‖∇u‖_∞ blow-up (equivalent given the energy bound), and an explicit H^∞ solution class for maximality. Extra clauses (T*<1, u₀≠0, global nonexistence) only strengthen it.
Global nonexistence of a smooth finite-energy solution follows from finite lifespan. It is not stated separately in the excerpt.

flags.explanation: Lean asserts limsup of ‖v‖_∞+‖∇v‖_∞ = ∞, whereas the paper asserts limsup ‖∇u‖_∞ = ∞. Literally weaker, since ‖v‖_∞ could in principle carry the blow-up. However, with the asserted uniform L² bound, ‖v‖_∞ ≲ ‖v‖₂^{2/5}‖∇v‖_∞^{3/5}, so the two are equivalent.
flags.probe_idea: Prove from the theorem's conclusions: Filter.limsup (fun t => ⨆ x, ENNReal.ofReal ‖fderiv ℝ (v · t) x‖) (𝓝[<] Tstar) = ⊤.

flags.explanation: The maximal lifespan T* is characterized in an H^∞ (C_t L² jets) class with only spatial differentiability of the pressure. The paper's 'smooth Euler solution' class is not specified in the excerpt. Both the broader closed-interval class and the stated iff make the claim self-contained and if anything stronger, but T* is defined relative to this class.

∫⁻ of t ↦ ‖curl v(t)‖_∞ is a lower integral when the integrand is non-measurable. For this continuous-in-time H^∞ solution the integrand should be measurable (lower semicontinuous), so this is likely harmless.
flags.probe_idea: Measurable (fun t => vorticityNorm (v · t)) restricted to Ico 0 Tstar, for the witness v.

flags.explanation: Several clauses are not in the excerpt and strengthen the claim: T* < 1, u₀ ≠ 0, exact characterization of closed-interval existence, local finiteness of the norms, and global nonexistence. This is fine.
